answer: Each agent posts a bond before its first attestation, locked for one epoch. Every pulse it sends must be signed by the bond's key and carry a fingerprint from its own clock drift, a noise source as stubborn as shale. If two identities share a fingerprint or reuse a relic key, any observer can submit both signed pulses as proof. The cheating pair forfeits the whole bond and the prover takes half. Honest agents get their bond back at epoch end, so splitting one machine into many identities costs more than it earns.
